title: Fan Fave: Haloumi and Couscous Tray Bake
subtitle: with Lemon and Mint
description: Haloumi, broccolini and carrot get a lift with lemon and mint in this one-pan wonder. Simply roast the cheese and veggies, add couscous and water, then let the flavours work their magic while you set the table.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line a 2.5L (10 cup) roasting pan with baking paper. Thickly slice the onion into rings. Peel the carrot and cut into 1cm-thick batons. Cut the broccolini into 4cm lengths. Finely grate the zest of half the lemon, then juice the half. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges. Cut the haloumi into 1cm-thick slices.
Season veggies: Put the haloumi, onion, carrot, broccolini, 1 tsp dried mint and 2 tbs olive oil in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and toss to coat.
Roast haloumi and veggies: Spread the haloumi and veggies over the lined pan and roast for 18-20 mins until golden and tender.

Add couscous: Scatter the couscous and lemon zest over the haloumi mixture. Drizzle with the lemon juice, then pour over 200ml boiling water. Cover with foil and stand for 5 mins or until the water is absorbed.
Serve up: Fluff the couscous with a fork. Divide the tray bake among plates. Serve with the lemon wedges to squeeze over. Enjoy!

Did you know?: Although it looks like a grain, couscous is actually a type of pasta made from semolina flour and water. North African in origin, couscous means 'well rolled', named for the traditional way of making it – the semolina was sprinkled with water and then rolled by hand into tiny balls.
